region: Dundee · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Hermann J. Wiemer grew up in Bernkastel, in Germany’s Mosel Valley, in a family long rooted in winemaking. In the Finger Lakes he recognized the Mosel’s cool climate and gravelly soils, and in 1973 he bought a former soybean field on the west side of Seneca Lake. He started a grafting nursery in 1974, founded the winery in 1979 and became one of the region’s great pioneers of dry Riesling. Since his retirement in 2007 the estate has been run by Fred Merwarth, his former apprentice, and Swedish agronomist Oskar Bynke.

Wiemer was already making traditional-method sparkling wine in the 1980s, when dry Riesling was still a hard sell in America. The Extra Brut is 100% Riesling from the estate’s Magdalena and Standing Stone vineyards on Seneca Lake. The grapes are picked and sorted by hand, pressed as whole clusters and fermented with native yeasts; after the second fermentation in bottle the wine spends 30 months en tirage before being riddled and disgorged by hand. Vintage-dated from 2015 to 2018, it is now a non-vintage blend of several years, finished with just 5 g/l of dosage.

Riesling’s high, structural acidity is the point here; Merwarth says these wines “will go forever.” The winery describes lively acidity, fresh citrus peel, chalky minerality and a taut, crisp mousse, and points to seafood, his own favorite match being crab cakes. The estate farms without herbicides and with a biodynamic approach, and the wine is unfined and vegan.
facts: Traditional method; native-yeast fermentation, hand-riddled and hand-disgorged
